subject.purpose: Define the minimum topology, interfaces, trust boundaries, operational checks, and pre-execution confirmations for one bounded infrastructure or network change.

applicability.rationale: A compact contract is sufficient when topology, interfaces, authority, recovery, and verification matter but a full software State–Decision–Effect model does not.

stateDecisionEffect.rationale: No independently evolving semantic product state is introduced by this bounded configuration contract.
stateDecisionEffect.trigger: Reassess if retries, ambiguous acknowledgement, concurrent mutation, or durable semantic state becomes material.

migration.rationale: Configuration replacement and rollback touchpoints must be named.

failureRecovery.rationale: Connectivity and configuration changes require containment and rollback.

securityTrust.rationale: The contract crosses a network or trust boundary.

preExecutionConfirmation.rationale: Exact node, platform, policy, and tool facts must be confirmed before effects.

artifactTopology.responsibility: Hold parameterized configuration and rollback material for the bounded infrastructure change.

keyContracts.name: Bounded connectivity contract
keyContracts.shape: source, destination, transport, authorization, expected observation, failure behavior
keyContracts.responsibility: Define the exact permitted communication path and prevent implicit broad exposure.
invariants: Only declared peers and routes are permitted.
failureSemantics: A failed or ambiguous connection does not broaden routing or authority.

behaviorPaths.name: Apply, verify, and safely reverse configuration
behaviorPaths.trigger: Authorized execution of this bounded configuration

steps.interaction: Apply through the declared owner and effect boundary.
Observe exact success criteria; roll back on failed or ambiguous results.

behaviorPaths.success: Required connectivity and isolation observations are established.
failureAndRecovery: Preserve prior configuration, stop affected traffic, and restore the last known-good state.

effectBoundaries.authorization: Exact effect grant for the named node or service
effectBoundaries.idempotency: Use compare-before-write or a documented safe replay strategy.
effectBoundaries.failure: Partial or ambiguous application may disrupt connectivity.
effectBoundaries.recovery: Restore the captured pre-state or execute the bound rollback procedure.

testSeams.statement: Verify declared reachability and explicit denial from the exact affected nodes.

observabilityPoints.statement: Record active configuration, service health, route or policy state, and endpoint observations.

migrationTouchpoints.statement: Capture pre-state and define a tested rollback or successor configuration path.

fixed.statement: Only explicitly declared nodes, routes, interfaces, and effects are in scope.
fixed.rationale: Prevents a compact infrastructure contract from becoming a flat implicit network grant.
fixed.changeRoute: Return material topology, trust-boundary, or authority changes to the responsible planning owner.

delegated.area: Private configuration syntax and local sequencing
delegated.bounds: May vary when it preserves the declared topology, interfaces, trust boundaries, effects, checks, and rollback.

prohibited: Do not broaden network exposure, credentials, effects, or authority through an implementation convenience.

preExecutionConfirmations.statement: Confirm exact node identities, operating systems or firmware, interfaces, addresses, and administrative owners.
preExecutionConfirmations.method: Authenticated inventory or bounded read-only inspection of every target node
preExecutionConfirmations.reopenTrigger: Any node, interface, or platform changes.

preExecutionConfirmations.statement: Confirm applicable egress, ingress, firewall, certificate, credential, and external-owner restrictions.
preExecutionConfirmations.method: Authoritative policy source or bounded endpoint probe
preExecutionConfirmations.reopenTrigger: Policy, network, certificate, or endpoint changes.

acceptanceCriteria: Topology, interfaces, trust boundaries, effects, and rollback are explicit.
Pre-execution confirmations identify every material unknown and owner.
No unverified command or platform behavior is represented as exact.
